arguments.body: Hi Jonah, it's Mare and Co. We've sent an emergency locksmith (Hackney Locks 24/7) to 27 Bethnal Green Road; target arrival tonight between 9.30pm and 11.30pm. Please stay somewhere warm nearby and keep your phone on, they may call you. Don't pay anything tonight: the landlord's pre-approved emergency cover applies, and the locksmith's report will decide whether any cost is recharged. Your earlier stiff-lock report (R-4766) is linked to this job. Spare keys are only collectable in office hours (Mon-Fri 9-17.30, £50 refundable deposit), so the locksmith is the quickest route. If you feel unsafe, call 999. We'll update you by email tomorrow.

Dear Margaret, tonight your tenant at 27 Bethnal Green Road was locked out after the key snapped in the front door lock (half still in it). He had reported the lock as stiff on 22 Sept (R-4766). As a vulnerable tenant outside at night, we've sent Hackney Locks 24/7 as an emergency under your standing instruction. Cause is unconfirmed; the locksmith's report will decide whether it's a lock fault (your cost) or tenant damage. We'll send you the report and cost once we have them.

arguments.summary: Vulnerable tenant locked out at night after key snapped; he had reported a stiff lock on 22 Sept (R-4766, unactioned). I dispatched the on-call locksmith under the landlord's standing emergency approval, told tenant and landlord, and escalated P1 for human confirmation of attendance.

answers.question: Is this a tenant-responsibility lockout or a landlord-responsibility lock fault? What is still uncertain?
answers.answer: Probably not a simple lost-key lockout: a key snapped in a lock reported stiff for weeks (R-4766), which points to a lock fault, a landlord responsibility. Uncertain: whether wear or tenant misuse caused it. Policy says the locksmith's report decides the recharge.

answers.question: What options do you give the tenant tonight and who pays for each?
answers.answer: 1) Emergency locksmith tonight (dispatched): landlord covers the call-out under standing emergency approval, with any recharge to the tenant decided only after the report. 2) Spare key from office: only Mon-Fri 9-17.30 with a £50 refundable deposit, so not available tonight. The master key is not a tonight option and would not remove the snapped key anyway.

answers.question: What actions do you take?
answers.answer: Assigned Hackney Locks 24/7 (A1), updated the ticket (A2), texted the tenant (A3), emailed the landlord (A4), and escalated P1 to confirm attendance (A5).

conflicts: Tenant said he reported the lock on the portal 'I think'; ticket R-4766 (22 Sept, stage init) confirms it. The tenant's belief that the master key is available conflicts with the policy, which allows it in office hours only.
assumptions: Landlord note 'Approve emergencies without asking' covers an out-of-hours lockout of a vulnerable tenant
The tenant's cost recharge, if any, is decided later from the locksmith report
